title: Release Bridge Call — Playback & Risk Scan (2025-02-18)
summary: Playback of the 02/18 release bridge call covering runtime v2.4.1 rollout plan, CANARY run in us-east-1, hotfix candidates, and a rapid risk-scan for known unknowns. Primary goal: staged release with safe rollback options if KV cache latency or tokenization regression reappears. This doc captures decisions, open questions, and owners for the next 72 hours.
agenda: Quick health check and known incidents
notes:
09:05 PST start. Quick state: production stable overnight; sporadic CPU spikes reported in eu-west-1 (investigating separate). Release window approved 10:00–14:00 PST. Runtime v2.4.1 includes attention optimization, KV-cache prefetch change, and batching tweak.

Canary plan: 2 canary hosts in us-east-1 behind the regular LB, target 5% of incoming traffic for first 30 minutes, then 20% for next 60 minutes if metrics stable. Metrics to watch: p95 latency, token/second throughput, error rate, model output divergence score (auto-eval on a small prompt set). Canary gating thresholds: p95 < 130ms (+10% baseline), error-rate < 0.5%, divergence delta < 2.5 BLEU-equivalent metric.

Observed regression vector: the KV-cache prefetch change reduced cold-start latency but introduced a slow warmup path for long-sequence requests. QA reproduced the slow-warmup at scale in staging: median warmup time 2.9s (target <1.2s) when sequence>2048. Mitigation discussed: pre-warm script to prime KV entries before traffic shift and temporarily increase kv-prefetch-batch-size. Alejandro to prepare canary environment with pre-warm hook.

Hotfix candidates: PR #2347 (revert aggressive prefetch heuristics) is ready for fast patch. If canary p95 > 150ms or error-rate spikes > 1.0% in first 30 minutes, immediate action: revert to previous prefetch heuristics (hotfix path A) and shift canary traffic back to 0% while scaling classic runtime pool. Escalation: call SRE lead and release lead; page oncall.

Rollout decisions: proceed with staged canary today per plan. Hold condition: any model-output regression above threshold or persistent kv-warmup > 1.5s after pre-warm attempt. If hold occurs, open incident and break release for deeper analysis.

Communications: update #release-bridge Slack with minute-by-minute short bullets during rollout. Customer-facing status page will be updated only if rollback occurs or customer-impacting errors detected.

Open questions captured during call: 1) Are there any downstream consumers of the KV cache that rely on ordering semantics changed by prefetch? (Action: Priya to confirm with model-onboarding team). 2) Can we synthetic-exercise heavy long-sequence workload on canary before shifting live traffic? (Action: Derek to run load script).
risk_scan: KV-cache warmup regression (Severity: High) — Likelihood: Medium. Mitigation: pre-warm hook + fallback revert PR #2347. Owner: Alejandro. Contingency: rollback within 10 minutes.
Model tokenization divergence (Severity: High) — Likelihood: Low but impact high. Mitigation: run quick eval set during canary; if divergence > threshold, abort. Owner: Derek.
Autoscale lag under burst (Severity: Medium) — Likelihood: Medium. Mitigation: pre-provision burst capacity in us-east-1 for release window. Owner: Chen.
Config drift between regions (Severity: Medium) — Likelihood: Low. Mitigation: checksum of runtime configs pre-rollout. Owner: Maya.
Monitoring breakage / missing traces (Severity: Medium) — Likelihood: Low. Mitigation: sanity check telemetry pipelines 30m before shift. Owner: Samira.
Customer-visible higher cost due to mis-batching (Severity: Low) — Likelihood: Medium. Mitigation: revert batching flag if cost/perf delta > 15%. Owner: Product Ops (Priya).

Derek: Run long-sequence synthetic load on canary (script: load-longseq-v3) and post results to this doc (due 2025-02-18 09:30 PST)
Chen: Provision + confirm burst capacity in us-east-1 and validate autoscaler lookback window (due 2025-02-18 09:50 PST)
Priya: Confirm no downstream ordering dependencies in model-onboarding/team and update linked artifact if there are (due 2025-02-18 09:40 PST)
Samira: Run telemetry sanity check for traces, metrics, and logs; confirm dashboards are receiving canary tags (due 2025-02-18 09:35 PST)
Maya: Publish minute-by-minute Slack guide and hold contact list; be primary comms until handoff (due 2025-02-18 09:15 PST)
Maya: If rollback triggered, open incident in PagerDuty and file postmortem stub (due immediate on rollback)
All: Confirm readiness in #release-bridge 10 minutes prior to shift (due 2025-02-18 09:50 PST)
change_log_summary:
runtime v2.4.1: attention kernel micro-optimizations (+6-9% throughput on short context),
kv-cache prefetch change to reduce cold-starts, batch sizing tweak for cont-batching
config flags: kv-prefetch-batch-size default bumped from 8->24 in v2.4.1 (can be overridden at runtime via feature flag)
metric hooks: added model-output-divergence quick-eval endpoint and canary tagging headers
packaging: new docker base image with glibc 2.36 (minor OS-level perf gain)
follow_up_meeting: If rollout succeeds, quick sync 2025-02-18 15:30 PST to confirm metrics and close ticket. If rollback occurs, convene incident review within 48 hours.
post_notes: Post-call: Derek found a flaky test that overestimated warmup time; adjusted load script and re-ran. Alejandro pushed canary with pre-warm hook and initial synthetic passed. Monitoring flagged a transient p95 blip at 10:12 PST — investigated, attributed to queue backlog in lb; spin-up of extra canary host cleared backlog. No rollback performed. Will track extended warmup regression in the 48h window.
